tools.name: Add a comment to a file
tools.description: Posts a new comment to a Figma file or branch, optionally replying to an existing root comment (replies cannot be nested); `region_height` and `region_width` in `client_meta` must be positive if defining a comment region.

inputs.name: message
inputs.about: Text content of the comment.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: Figma file key or branch key. Extract from the file URL: https://www.figma.com/design/FILE_KEY/... or https://www.figma.com/file/FILE_KEY/... The FILE_KEY is the alphanumeric string between 'design/' or 'file/' and the next slash. You must have access to the file (editor or commenter permissions req

inputs.name: comment_id
inputs.about: ID of an existing root comment to reply to. Replies cannot be made to other replies.

inputs.name: client_meta
inputs.about: Dictionary specifying the comment's position. Valid formats: 1) Absolute coordinates: {x, y} 2) Node-relative: {node_id, node_offset: {x, y}} (when node_id is used, coordinates MUST be inside node_offset) 3) Absolute region: {x, y, region_height, region_width, comment_pin_corner?} 4) Node-relative r

tools.name: Add a reaction to a comment
tools.description: Posts a specified emoji reaction to an existing comment in a Figma file or branch, requiring valid file_key and comment_id.

inputs.name: emoji
inputs.about: The emoji to use for the reaction, specified as a shortcode (e.g., `:heart:`, `:+1::skin-tone-2:`). For a comprehensive list of accepted emoji shortcodes, including aliases and skin tone modifiers, refer to the file linked here: [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/missive/emoji-mart/main/packages/emo

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: Identifier of the Figma file or branch to which the comment reaction will be posted. This can be a file key (e.g., from the file URL) or a branch key. Use the `GET /v1/files/:key` endpoint with the `branch_data=true` query parameter to obtain the branch key if needed.

inputs.name: comment_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the comment to which the reaction should be added.

tools.name: Create a webhook
tools.description: Creates a Figma webhook for team, project, or file events, sending POST notifications to the configured endpoint. Team webhooks require team admin permissions; project and file webhooks require edit access.

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: Initial webhook status. `ACTIVE` (default): webhook is operational and receives an initial PING event upon creation. `PAUSED`: webhook is inactive and receives no events; use FIGMA_UPDATE_A_WEBHOOK to activate later.

inputs.name: context
inputs.about: Scope of the webhook. Use with `context_id`. `team`: monitors all files in a team (requires team admin). `project`: monitors all files in a project (requires edit access). `file`: monitors a specific file (requires edit access). If not provided, `team_id` must be specified instead.

inputs.name: team_id
inputs.about: DEPRECATED: Use `context='team'` with `context_id` instead. Identifier of the Figma team for which this webhook monitors events. To find your team_id: navigate to your team page in Figma (https://www.figma.com/files/team/YOUR_TEAM_ID/Team-Name), the team_id is the number after '/team/' in the URL. N

inputs.name: endpoint
inputs.about: Publicly accessible HTTPS URL (max 2048 chars) that receives POST requests from Figma when the event triggers. Must be reachable from the internet. Figma sends JSON payloads with event details to this endpoint.

inputs.name: passcode
inputs.about: Secret string (max 100 chars) included in the webhook payload for verification. Use this to verify that incoming requests to your endpoint are genuinely from Figma.

inputs.name: context_id
inputs.about: ID of the context (team, project, or file) to monitor. For team: extract from URL https://www.figma.com/files/team/TEAM_ID/... For project: extract from URL or use FIGMA_GET_PROJECTS_IN_A_TEAM. For file: use the file_key from URL https://www.figma.com/design/FILE_KEY/... Required when `context` is s

inputs.name: event_type
inputs.about: Type of event that triggers the webhook. FILE_UPDATE: triggered when a file is saved/modified. FILE_DELETE: triggered when a file is deleted. FILE_VERSION_UPDATE: triggered when a new version is added to file history. FILE_COMMENT: triggered when a comment is added. LIBRARY_PUBLISH: triggered when a

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Optional human-readable description for the webhook (max 150 chars). Useful for identifying the webhook's purpose in the team's webhook list.

tools.name: Create dev resources
tools.description: Creates and attaches multiple uniquely-URLed development resources to specified Figma nodes, up to 10 per node.

inputs.name: dev_resources
inputs.about: List of development resources to create.

tools.name: Create, modify, or delete variables
tools.description: Manages variables, collections, modes, and their values in a Figma file via batch create/update/delete operations; use temporary IDs to link new related items in one request and ensure `variableModeValues` match the target variable's `resolvedType`.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: The key of the Figma file or branch to modify variables in. Use `GET /v1/files/:key` with the `branch_data=true` query parameter to obtain a branch key.

inputs.name: variables
inputs.about: List of operations for variables. Each item specifies an action (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE) and the relevant fields. Maximum 5000 variables per collection. Variables cannot be created in extended collections.

inputs.name: variableModes
inputs.about: List of operations for modes. Each item specifies an action (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE) and the relevant fields. Maximum 40 modes per collection. Modes cannot be created/updated in extended collections (only deleted if parent mode was deleted).

inputs.name: variableModeValues
inputs.about: List of value assignments for variables in specific modes. Each item sets the value of a variable in a particular mode. Values must match the variable's resolvedType.

inputs.name: variableCollections
inputs.about: List of operations for variable collections. Each item specifies an action (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE) and the relevant fields for that action.

tools.name: Delete a comment
tools.description: Deletes a specific comment from a Figma file or branch, provided the authenticated user is the original author of the comment.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: The key of the Figma file or branch from which the comment will be deleted. This can be a file key (typically found in the file's URL, e.g., 'sFHgQh9dL6369o5wrZHmdR' from https://www.figma.com/design/sFHgQh9dL6369o5wrZHmdR/...) or a branch key. To obtain a branch key, use the `GET /v1/files/:key` en

inputs.name: comment_id
inputs.about: The unique string identifier of the comment to be deleted. This ID can be obtained from the response of `GET /v1/files/:file_key/comments` or from the response when creating a comment with `POST /v1/files/:file_key/comments`. Only the author of the comment can delete it.

tools.name: Delete a reaction
tools.description: Deletes a specific emoji reaction from a comment in a Figma file; the user must have originally created the reaction.

inputs.name: emoji
inputs.about: The specific emoji character (e.g., '❤️', '👍') of the reaction to delete. This must be an exact match to the emoji of an existing reaction on the comment.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: Key of the file or branch containing the comment reaction to be deleted. The file key can be obtained from the file URL or API responses. To get a branch key, use the `GET /v1/files/:key` endpoint with the `branch_data` query parameter.

inputs.name: comment_id
inputs.about: Identifier of the comment from which the reaction will be removed. This ID is specific to the comment within the Figma file.

tools.name: Delete a webhook
tools.description: Permanently deletes an existing webhook, identified by its unique `webhook_id`; this operation is irreversible.

inputs.name: webhook_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the webhook to be deleted.

tools.name: Delete dev resource
tools.description: Deletes a development resource (used to link Figma design elements to external developer information like code or tasks) from a specified Figma file.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: Identifier of the Figma file from which to delete the dev resource. Must be a main file key, not a branch key.

inputs.name: dev_resource_id
inputs.about: Identifier of the dev resource to delete from the file.

tools.name: Design tokens to tailwind
tools.description: Converts design tokens into Tailwind CSS configuration content with theme extensions, and optionally generates global CSS with font imports.

inputs.name: prefix
inputs.about: Prefix for generated token names (e.g., 'brand-')

inputs.name: tokens
inputs.about: Design tokens object obtained from the FIGMA_EXTRACT_DESIGN_TOKENS action output. Contains colors, typography, spacing, border_radius, shadows, total_tokens, and sources.

inputs.name: config_format
inputs.about: Output format: 'ts' for TypeScript or 'js' for JavaScript

inputs.name: include_font_imports
inputs.about: Include @import statements for Google Fonts

tools.name: Detect Background Layers
tools.description: Detect background layers for selected nodes in a Figma file. This action analyzes the Figma document structure and identifies potential background elements for the given target nodes. It uses: - Geometric analysis (bounding box overlap/containment) - Z-index ordering (nodes earlier in the layer stack are behind later ones) - Visual properties (fills, node types) - Naming conventions (nodes named 'background', 'bg', etc.) Returns background candidates with confidence scores (0-1) and explanations.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: File key extracted from a Figma Design file URL. Example: 'abc123XYZ' from URL figma.com/design/abc123XYZ/My-Design. NOT supported: FigJam boards or Slides.

inputs.name: search_depth
inputs.about: How many levels up in the node hierarchy to search for backgrounds. Higher values find more distant ancestors but take longer. Default: 3.

inputs.name: target_node_ids
inputs.about: List of node IDs to find background layers for. Node IDs can be found in Figma URLs after 'node-id=' parameter, e.g., '1:2' or '123:456'. The action will search for potential background elements that are behind these target nodes.

tools.name: Discover Figma Resources
tools.description: Discovers Figma identifiers from supported file, design, board, prototype, slides, team and project URLs, and can list team projects, project files or file nodes. Project and file listing failures may appear as empty results.

inputs.name: team_id
inputs.about: Team ID to list all projects from. Get this from team URL: https://www.figma.com/files/team/YOUR_TEAM_ID/Team-Name. Returns list of projects with IDs and names. Cannot be inferred from user identity or FIGMA_GET_CURRENT_USER; must come from a team URL or be provided directly.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: File key to extract all node IDs from. Get this from file URL (figma.com/file/FILE_KEY/...) or from project files list. Returns hierarchical list of all nodes with IDs, names, types, and paths.

inputs.name: figma_url
inputs.about:
Full Figma URL to extract file_key, node_id, and team_id from. Works with any Figma URL format:
• File: https://www.figma.com/file/ABC123/Design-Name
• Design: https://www.figma.com/design/ABC123/Design-Name
• Board: https://www.figma.com/board/ABC123/Board-Name
• Prototype: https://www.figma.com/pr

inputs.name: max_depth
inputs.about: Maximum tree depth to traverse when discovering nodes. 2=pages+frames, 3=pages+frames+components, etc. Higher values find more nodes but take longer. Responses at depth 4+ or broad file_key traversal can exceed 20k tokens with significant latency; cap at 2–3 and target specific CANVAS or FRAME node

inputs.name: project_id
inputs.about: Project ID to list all files from. Get this from project URL or from team projects list. Returns files with keys, names, and thumbnails.

tools.name: Download Figma Images
tools.description: Download images from Figma file nodes. Renders specified nodes as images and downloads them. Supports PNG, SVG, JPG, and PDF formats. REQUIRED PARAMETERS: - file_key (string): The Figma file key from the URL - images (array): List of objects, each containing: - node_id (string, required): The node ID to export (e.g., "1:2") - file_name (string, required): Output filename with extension (e.g., "logo.png") - format (string, optional): One of 'png', 'svg', 'jpg', 'pdf'. Defaults to 'png' Example usage: { "file_key": "abc123XYZ", "images": [ {"node_id": "1:2", "file_name": "logo.png", "format": "png"} ] } To find node IDs, use FIGMA_GET_FILE_JSON or look in Figma URLs after 'node-id='. NOTE: Returned image URLs expire shortly after generation — download them immediately.

inputs.name: scale
inputs.about: Image scaling factor for PNG/JPG exports (0.01 to 4). Default is 2 for retina quality. Ignored for SVG/PDF. Exports are capped at ~32 megapixels; reduce scale or split large nodes to avoid hitting this limit.

inputs.name: images
inputs.about: REQUIRED. A list of image download requests. Each item must be an object with 'node_id' (string, required), 'file_name' (string, required), and optionally 'format' (string, defaults to 'png'). Example: [{"node_id": "1:2", "file_name": "logo.png"}]

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: REQUIRED. The Figma file key extracted from a Figma URL. For URL 'https://www.figma.com/file/abc123XYZ/MyDesign', the file_key is 'abc123XYZ'. This identifies which Figma file to download images from.

inputs.name: svg_include_id
inputs.about: For SVG exports only: include element IDs in the SVG output. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: svg_outline_text
inputs.about: For SVG exports only: convert text to paths for accurate rendering. Defaults to true.

inputs.name: svg_simplify_stroke
inputs.about: For SVG exports only: simplify strokes for cleaner SVG output. Defaults to true.

tools.name: Extract design tokens
tools.description: Extracts design tokens from a Figma file using styles, optional variables and node properties. Results may be incomplete or use fallback style values; variables require appropriate access and a supported plan.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: The Figma file key (e.g., 'aA1b2Cd3E4F5g6H7i8J9k0L'). Extract from Figma URLs like figma.com/file/FILE_KEY/... or use FIGMA_DISCOVER_FIGMA_RESOURCES to find file keys

inputs.name: include_variables
inputs.about: Include variables in extraction. Even with this enabled, modes and scopes may be incomplete; use FIGMA_GET_LOCAL_VARIABLES for full semantic token coverage including variable modes and aliases.

inputs.name: extract_from_nodes
inputs.about: Extract tokens from node properties

inputs.name: include_local_styles
inputs.about: Include local styles in extraction

tools.name: Extract Prototype Interactions
tools.description: Extract prototype interactions and animations from Figma files. Required parameter: - file_key: The Figma file key extracted from a URL like 'https://www.figma.com/file/ABC123xyz/MyFile' (the 'ABC123xyz' part) Analyzes the prototype data to extract: - User interactions (clicks, hovers, etc.) - Transition animations - Component variant states - User flows and navigation

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: Required. The unique file key from a Figma URL. To find it: from a URL like 'https://www.figma.com/file/ABC123xyz/MyFileName' or 'https://www.figma.com/design/ABC123xyz/MyFileName', extract the alphanumeric string after '/file/' or '/design/' (e.g., 'ABC123xyz'). This is typically 22 alphanumeric ch

inputs.name: analyze_components
inputs.about: Extract component variant states

inputs.name: include_animations
inputs.about: Include detailed animation data

tools.name: Get activity logs
tools.description: Retrieves Figma organization activity log events with event-type and time-range filters, ordering, and a page-size limit. Access requires an OAuth app and an Enterprise organization admin with the activity log scope.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Maximum number of events per response, for pagination. If unspecified, defaults to 1000.

inputs.name: order
inputs.about: Sort order for events by timestamp.

inputs.name: events
inputs.about: Comma-separated event types to include. If unspecified, all event types are returned. Refer to Figma's API documentation for a comprehensive list.

inputs.name: end_time
inputs.about: Unix timestamp for the latest time for events. If unspecified, defaults to the current timestamp.

inputs.name: start_time
inputs.about: Unix timestamp for the earliest time for events. If unspecified, defaults to one year ago.

tools.name: Get a webhook
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific webhook by its ID, provided the webhook exists and is accessible to the user.

inputs.name: webhook_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the webhook to retrieve.

tools.name: Get comments in a file
tools.description: Retrieves all comments from an existing Figma file, identified by a valid `file_key`, returning details like content, author, position, and reactions, with an option for Markdown formatted content.

inputs.name: as_md
inputs.about: If true, comment content will be returned in Markdown format where applicable (e.g., for links, bold text). Defaults to false, returning rich text structure.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: Identifier for the Figma file from which to retrieve comments. This can be a file key (a unique string identifying a file) or a branch key. To obtain a branch key, use the `GET /v1/files/:key` endpoint with the `branch_data` query parameter.

tools.name: Get component (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use FIGMA_GET_FILE_NODES instead. Get component data with automatic simplification. Returns clean, AI-friendly component structure.

inputs.name: node_id
inputs.about: ID of the component node. Must be a component node ID specifically (not a frame or page ID); pass verbatim from sources like FIGMA_GET_FILE_COMPONENTS.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: File key that contains the component

inputs.name: response_detail
inputs.about: Level of detail in the response. 'minimal' (default) simplifies component data for AI consumption. 'full' returns the raw Figma API response.

tools.name: Get component
tools.description: Fetches metadata for a specific component using its unique identifier. Use when you need to retrieve published component details from a team library.

inputs.name: key
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the component.

tools.name: Get component set
tools.description: Retrieves detailed metadata for a specific published Figma component set using its unique `key`.

inputs.name: key
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the component set.

tools.name: Get current user
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information for the currently authenticated Figma user.

tools.name: Get dev resources
tools.description: Retrieves development resources (e.g., Jira/GitHub links) for a Figma main file, optionally filtering by specific node IDs.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Figma design file from which to retrieve development resources. This must be the key for a main file, not a branch key. Extract the file_key from Figma URLs: figma.com/design/{file_key}/... or figma.com/file/{file_key}/...

inputs.name: node_ids
inputs.about: A comma-separated string of node IDs to filter dev resources. Example: '1:2,100:54'. If omitted, returns all dev resources in the file.

tools.name: Get file components
tools.description: Retrieves published components from a Figma file, which must be a main file (not a branch) acting as a library.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: Key of the Figma file. This file must be a main file (not a branch key) that acts as a library, as components are published from main files.

tools.name: Get file component sets
tools.description: Retrieves all published component sets from the specified Figma main file (file_key must not be for a branch).

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: Key of the Figma file. Must be a main file key (not a branch key) as component sets are published from main files. Extract from Figma URL: https://www.figma.com/design/{file_key}/... or https://www.figma.com/file/{file_key}/...

tools.name: Get file json
tools.description: Retrieves data for a Figma Design file or selected nodes, with options to specify a version and limit tree depth. By default it returns a simplified view that omits invisible nodes and empty values; choose full detail for the raw Figma response. Use node IDs and depth to reduce response size for large files.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated node IDs to fetch specific nodes (uses /nodes endpoint). Node IDs can be extracted from Figma URLs: figma.com/design/{file_key}/{name}?node-id={node_id}. Example: '1:2,1:3' for multiple nodes. Must be a string, not an array — passing an array causes validation failure. URL node IDs u

inputs.name: depth
inputs.about: Tree traversal depth (e.g., 2 for pages and top-level children). Omitting depth on large files can produce extremely large responses or timeouts; scope with `ids` and set depth to the minimum needed.

inputs.name: version
inputs.about: Specific version ID; current version if omitted

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: File key extracted from a Figma Design file URL. SUPPORTED: figma.com/design/{file_key}/... or figma.com/file/{file_key}/... NOT SUPPORTED: FigJam boards (figma.com/board/{file_key}) and Slides (figma.com/slides/{file_key}). Example valid key: 'abc123XYZ' from URL figma.com/design/abc123XYZ/My-Desig

inputs.name: geometry
inputs.about: Set to "paths" to include vector data

inputs.name: branch_data
inputs.about: Include branch metadata

inputs.name: plugin_data
inputs.about: Comma-separated plugin IDs to include plugin data

inputs.name: response_detail
inputs.about: Level of detail in the response. 'minimal' (default) simplifies file data for AI consumption. 'full' returns the raw Figma API response.

tools.name: Get file metadata
tools.description: Get Figma file metadata including name, creator, last modification details, thumbnail, and access information. Use when you need quick file overview without the full document tree.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: File key to get metadata for. This can be a file key or branch key. Extract from file URL: https://www.figma.com/design/{file_key}/... or https://www.figma.com/file/{file_key}/... Use `GET /v1/files/:key` with the `branch_data` query param to get the branch key.

tools.name: Get file nodes
tools.description: Fetch JSON for specific node IDs from a Figma file to avoid full-file payload limits. Use when you already know target node IDs (from shallow file fetch or component listings) or when full-file JSON has hit payload limits. Prefer depth=1 for fast discovery.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Node IDs to retrieve. Provide as comma-separated string (e.g., '1:5,1:6') or as list of strings (e.g., ['1:5', '1:6']). Use this when you already know target node IDs from a shallow file fetch or component/style listings.

inputs.name: depth
inputs.about: How deep into each requested node subtree to traverse. Use depth=1 for fast structure discovery (only immediate children), increase only when needed. Omit to get full subtree.

inputs.name: version
inputs.about: Specific version ID to retrieve. Omit for current version.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: Figma file key or branch key extracted from URL. Example: 'abc123XYZ' from figma.com/design/abc123XYZ/My-Design.

inputs.name: geometry
inputs.about: Set to 'paths' to include vector path data in the response. Omit for standard node data without geometry.

inputs.name: plugin_data
inputs.about: Plugin IDs (comma-separated) or 'shared' to include plugin data. Omit to exclude plugin data.

tools.name: Get files in a project
tools.description: Lists files in a Figma project, optionally including metadata for branches of main files. DEPRECATED: Figma recommends the folders endpoint GET /v2/folders/:folder_id/files instead; existing integrations are unaffected.

inputs.name: project_id
inputs.about: Identifier of the Figma project, typically found in its URL.

inputs.name: branch_data
inputs.about: If true, includes metadata for branches of main files.

tools.name: Get file styles
tools.description: Retrieves a list of published styles (like colors, text attributes, effects, and layout grids) from a specified main Figma file (not a branch).

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: Key of the main Figma file (not a branch) from which to retrieve published styles. Extract the file_key from the Figma URL: figma.com/design/{file_key}/... or figma.com/file/{file_key}/... Note: This endpoint only returns PUBLISHED styles from team libraries. For local/unpublished styles, use FIGMA_

tools.name: Get image fills
tools.description: Retrieves temporary (14-day expiry) download URLs for all image fills in a Figma file; requires `imageRef` from `Paint` objects to map URLs.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: The unique identifier of a Figma file. Extract this from Figma URLs: https://www.figma.com/file/{file_key}/... or https://www.figma.com/design/{file_key}/... The file_key is a 22-character alphanumeric string (e.g., 'sFHgQh9dL6369o5wrZHmdR').

tools.name: Get library analytics component action data
tools.description: Retrieves component insertion and detachment analytics for a specified Figma library, groupable by 'component' or 'team' and filterable by a date range (YYYY-MM-DD).

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: Opaque cursor for pagination, from a previous response's `cursor` field; omit for the first page.

inputs.name: end_date
inputs.about: End date (YYYY-MM-DD) for analytics. Data includes up to end of this date's week. Defaults to latest computed week.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: Unique identifier (key) of the Figma library file to retrieve analytics data from. Must be a published library file from an Enterprise plan organization.

inputs.name: group_by
inputs.about: Dimension to group analytics: 'component' or 'team'.

inputs.name: start_date
inputs.about: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD) for analytics. Data includes from start of this date's week. Defaults to one year prior.

tools.name: Get library analytics component usage data
tools.description: Retrieves component usage analytics for a specified Figma library file (identified by `file_key`), with data groupable by 'component' or 'file'.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: Opaque string for pagination to fetch the next page of data, obtained from a previous response.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: Unique identifier (key) of the Figma library file. Must be a published library file from an Enterprise plan organization.

inputs.name: group_by
inputs.about: Dimension to group analytics data, affecting the response `rows` structure. Use 'component' to see per-component usage stats, or 'file' to see which files use the library.

tools.name: Get library analytics style action data
tools.description: Retrieves style usage analytics (insertions, detachments) for a Figma library, grouped by 'style' or 'team'; if providing a date range, ensure end_date is not before start_date.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: Opaque cursor for pagination, from a previous response's `cursor` field to fetch the next page; omit for first page.

inputs.name: end_date
inputs.about: End date for the analytics data range (YYYY-MM-DD). Data includes up to the end of this date's week. Defaults to the most recently computed week if unspecified.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: Unique identifier (key) of the Figma library. Must be a published library file from an Enterprise plan organization.

inputs.name: group_by
inputs.about: Dimension by which to group the library style analytics data. Use 'style' for per-style metrics or 'team' for per-team metrics.

inputs.name: start_date
inputs.about: Start date for the analytics data range (YYYY-MM-DD). Data includes from the start of this date's week. Defaults to one year prior if unspecified.

tools.name: Get library analytics style usage data
tools.description: Retrieves style usage analytics for a published Figma library. Returns data about how styles (colors, text styles, effects, grids) from the library are being used across your organization. Requires Enterprise plan and library_analytics:read scope. Group results by 'style' to see per-style metrics or by 'file' to see which files use the library's styles.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: Pagination cursor from a previous response's 'cursor' field. Omit to get the first page of results.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: The unique file key of a published Figma library. Obtain this from the library URL (e.g., figma.com/file/FILE_KEY/...) or via the Get Team Styles endpoint. Note: This API is only available on Enterprise plans.

inputs.name: group_by
inputs.about: How to group the analytics data: 'style' returns usage stats per style, 'file' returns usage stats per file using the library.

tools.name: Get library analytics variable action data
tools.description: Retrieves weekly, paginated analytics data on variable insertions and detachments for a specified Figma library (identified by `file_key`), groupable by 'variable' or 'team', and filterable by an optional date range. Note: Requires Enterprise plan and library_analytics:read scope.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: Opaque cursor for pagination from a previous response; omit or use null for the first page.

inputs.name: end_date
inputs.about: End date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the analytics range. Data is aggregated weekly; this date rounds to the nearest week end. Defaults to the latest computed week if unspecified.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: Unique identifier (key) of the Figma file (library) for which to retrieve variable analytics data.

inputs.name: group_by
inputs.about: Dimension to group analytics data, which determines the structure of `rows` in the response.

inputs.name: start_date

tools.name: Get payments

inputs.name: widget_id

inputs.name: community_file_id

inputs.name: plugin_payment_token
inputs.about: Short-lived auth token from `getPluginPaymentTokenAsync` (Figma Plugin Payments API). See Figma docs 'Calling the Payments REST API...'. If provided, `user_id` and resource IDs are typically not needed.

tools.name: Get reactions for a comment

tools.name: Get SCIM service provider config
tools.description: Get Figma's SCIM service provider configuration. Returns configuration details including which SCIM operations are supported (patch, bulk, filter, etc.), authentication schemes, and service capabilities.

tools.name: Get style

inputs.about: The unique identifier (key) of the style to retrieve. Style keys are 40-character hexadecimal hash strings obtained from the GET /v1/files/{file_key}/styles or GET /v1/teams/{team_id}/styles endpoints. This endpoint only works for styles published in a team library.

tools.description: Retrieves a paginated list of published component sets (collections of reusable UI elements) from a specified Figma team's library.

tools.name: Get team styles
tools.description: Retrieves a paginated list of published styles (fill colors, text styles, effects, grids) from a specified Figma team's library. Note: The team must have published styles in its library for this endpoint to return data. Teams without published styles will return an empty list.

inputs.name: after
inputs.about: Opaque integer cursor to retrieve styles after this point; use `cursor.after` from a previous response. Mutually exclusive with `before` - only one can be specified.

inputs.about: Opaque integer cursor to retrieve styles before this point; use `cursor.before` from a previous response. Mutually exclusive with `after` - only one can be specified.

inputs.name: page_size
inputs.about: Number of style items to return per page. Maximum supported value is 100.

tools.description: Retrieves webhooks registered for a specified Figma team, project, or file context using the Webhooks V2 API.

Note: team_id cannot be programmatically obtained from the API - extract it from your Figma team URL: https://www.figma.com/f

Extract from file URL: https://www.figma.com/design/{file_key}/... or https://www.figma.com/file/{file_key}/... For branch keys, use `GET /v1/files/:key` with the `branch_data` query param to obtain it. The authenticated

inputs.name: page_size

tools.name: Get webhook requests
tools.description: Retrieves a history of webhook requests for a specific Figma webhook subscription; data is available for requests sent within the last seven days.

inputs.name: webhook_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Figma webhook subscription for which to retrieve past event requests. This refers to the ID of the webhook itself, not an individual event.

tools.name: Render images of file nodes
tools.description: Render Figma nodes as images (PNG, JPG, SVG, PDF). Returns a map of node IDs to temporary image URLs (valid for 30 days). Images are capped at 32 megapixels; larger requests are automatically scaled down. REQUIRED PARAMETERS: - file_key: Figma file key from URL (e.g., 'abc123XYZ' from figma.com/design/abc123XYZ/...) - ids: Comma-separated node IDs to render (e.g., '1:2' or '1:2,1:3,1:4') NODE IDs: Found in Figma URLs after 'node-id=' or from FIGMA_GET_FILE_JSON response. FORMATS: - png/jpg: Raster images with optional scale (0.01-4.0) - svg: Vector graphics with text outline options - pdf: Document format COMMON ISSUES: - null value in images map = node failed to render (invalid ID, invisible, 0% opacity) - 404 error = file_key not found or no access - 429 error = rate limit exceeded, wait and retry

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of node IDs to render as images. Node IDs are found in Figma URLs after 'node-id=' (e.g., '1:2') or from FIGMA_GET_FILE_JSON response. Example: '1:2,1:3,1:4'.

inputs.name: scale
inputs.about: Image scaling factor between 0.01 and 4.0. Example: 2.0 renders at 2x resolution. Applies to PNG/JPG only; ignored for SVG/PDF.

inputs.name: format
inputs.about: Output image format: 'png', 'jpg', 'svg', or 'pdf'.

inputs.name: version
inputs.about: Specific version ID of the file to render. If omitted, uses current version.

inputs.name: file_key
inputs.about: Key of the Figma file or branch. Extract from Figma URLs: figma.com/design/{file_key}/... or figma.com/file/{file_key}/... For branch keys, use GET /v1/files/:key with branch_data=true.

inputs.name: contents_only
inputs.about: If true, excludes content that overlaps node boundaries. If false, includes overlapping content (may increase processing time).

inputs.name: svg_include_id
inputs.about: (SVG only) If true, includes 'id' attributes (using layer names) on SVG elements.

inputs.name: svg_outline_text
inputs.about: (SVG only) If true, text renders as vector paths (outlines) for exact visual fidelity. If false, text renders as <text> elements (selectable, but appearance may vary by system fonts).

inputs.name: svg_include_node_id
inputs.about: (SVG only) If true, adds 'data-node-id' attribute (with Figma node ID) to SVG elements.

inputs.name: svg_simplify_stroke
inputs.about: (SVG only) If true, simplifies strokes using 'stroke' attribute instead of <mask>.

inputs.name: use_absolute_bounds
inputs.about: If true, uses full node dimensions ignoring cropping/empty space. Useful for text nodes to avoid unintended cropping.

tools.name: Update a webhook
tools.description: Updates an existing Figma webhook, identified by `webhook_id`, allowing modification of its event type, endpoint, passcode, status, or description.

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: Operational status: `ACTIVE` to receive events, `PAUSED` to temporarily stop event delivery. Optional - only provide to change status.

inputs.name: endpoint
inputs.about: URL of the HTTPS endpoint to receive POST requests for webhook events. Max length 2048. Optional - only provide to change the endpoint.

inputs.name: passcode
inputs.about: Secret string for your endpoint to verify webhook authenticity. Max length 100. Optional - only provide to change the passcode.

inputs.name: event_type
inputs.about: Type of event that triggers the webhook. Optional - only provide to change the event type.

inputs.name: webhook_id
inputs.about: Unique identifier of the existing webhook to update. Obtain from GET team webhooks or after creating a webhook.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: User-friendly description for the webhook. Max length 140 characters. Pass empty string to remove. Optional.

tools.name: Update dev resources
tools.description: Updates the name and/or URL of one or more existing Figma Dev Resources, each identified by its unique `id`.

inputs.name: dev_resources
inputs.about: List of dev resources to update. Each must include its `id` and can optionally provide a new `name` and/or `url`.
